title: ProbeAnswer
description: The JSON object the MODEL is asked to emit inside the single ```json fence of a checkpoint reply (protocol.PROBE_TEXT). This is the raw payload, not a derived row — probes.schema.json describes the row that wraps it. A payload validating here is exactly what lib/wur/protocol.py:parse_answer() calls parse_tier "strict"; protocol.py:strict_answer_errors() re-implements these rules in stdlib Python because the driver runs on a python3 with no jsonschema. Changing either one requires changing the other.

probe_id.description: Echoed back verbatim from the probe, so answer<->probe attribution is exact rather than positional. Minted by protocol.probe_id(run_id, k) = 'WURP-' + sha256(run_id)[:8] + '-' + k:03d.

facts.description: Exactly 3 slots. With one fact per task at least 2 are filler by construction — the filler distribution is itself a finding, not noise. An entry the model cannot fill honestly uses the literal string "NONE" for both fact and source.

source.description: file path | tool call | task prompt, or the literal "NONE". Checked against the run's workspace to set slots[].source_verified.

affects_next_action.description: The model's own claim that this fact drives its next move. Compared against the actually-issued next tool call to give probe fidelity.

next_action.description: The single next thing the model says it will do. The other half of the probe-fidelity comparison.
